name: Trendione
lead: Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar') is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement.[1]

It is inactive itself, with more than 100-fold lower affinity than trenbolone for androgen and progesterone receptors.[1] Most published work on it concerns environmental fate: trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant, and trendione is excreted in manure.[2][3] It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1]
infobox: Listed in the 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act (per Wikipedia)

paras: Wikipedia compares trendione to androstenedione's relationship with testosterone: a precursor expected to convert to the active steroid in the body. In receptor assays it has far weaker binding than trenbolone.[1]

Studies of cattle implanted with trenbolone acetate identify 17alpha-trenbolone and trendione as main metabolites in manure. Research has examined how they degrade in agricultural soils, sorb to soil and break down under light.[2][3]
No studies found. Published work is limited to laboratory receptor assays and environmental studies.

card.summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold as a prohormone; studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.
card.note: Listed in the US 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act.

quick.overview:
Trendione is a trenbolone metabolite that has been sold online as a prohormone supplement. It is listed in the US 2014 designer steroid law.

No human studies exist.
quick.mechanism: It is inactive by itself in receptor assays; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone.
quick.risks: No human safety data. Legal restrictions apply in the US.
